description: Empowering astronauts to safeguard their health in deep space! As part of the NASA Space Apps Challenge, our team is developing an intelligent health monitoring system designed to analyze health indicators in real-time, enabling crew members to self-evaluate, mitigate spaceflight hazards, and thrive during long-duration missions.
summary:
We developed an AI-powered platform for monitoring astronaut health and spacecraft environmental conditions during long-duration space missions.

The platform tracks physiological indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen saturation, respiration, and body temperature, alongside environmental factors such as CO2, oxygen levels, air pressure, humidity, and radiation exposure.

Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning models, the system analyzes data patterns, monitors changes over time, and identifies potential abnormalities. It also uses personalized health baselines to evaluate changes according to each astronaut's individual condition. A dedicated Decision Engine translates analysis results into understandable risk assessments and initial first-aid guidance.

By connecting astronaut health with spacecraft environmental monitoring, our solution aims to improve risk awareness, support informed decision-making, and help astronauts respond to potential health concerns when immediate medical assistance is limited.
details:
Our project is an AI-powered astronaut health and spacecraft environment monitoring platform designed to support astronaut safety during long-duration space missions.

How It Works:

The system monitors two interconnected dimensions: astronaut health and spacecraft environmental conditions.

For astronaut health, it tracks indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, SpO2, respiration rate, body temperature, blood glucose, and intraocular pressure. For the spacecraft, it monitors temperature, humidity, internal air pressure, CO2, oxygen levels, and radiation exposure.

The system uses multiple Machine Learning and Deep Learning models to analyze patterns, monitor changes over time, and identify potential abnormalities. It also incorporates personalized health baselines, allowing the system to evaluate changes according to each astronaut's individual condition rather than relying exclusively on fixed thresholds.

A dedicated Decision Engine processes the analysis outputs and provides understandable risk assessments, initial first-aid guidance, and recommended actions.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

  • Supports continuous monitoring of astronaut health and spacecraft environmental conditions.
  • Improves awareness of potential health and environmental risks.
  • Uses personalized baselines to make monitoring more relevant to each astronaut.
  • Helps astronauts understand their health status and make informed decisions.
  • Provides initial guidance when immediate medical assistance may be limited.

Technologies and Tools:

  • Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and React.js.
  • Backend: Express.js.
  • AI and Machine Learning: Python.
  • Model Training and Experimentation: Google Colab.
  • AI Models: VAE-BiLSTM-MHA, PatchTST, Transformer Encoder, XGBoost Classifier, Isolation Forest, and Bi-LSTM with Attention.
  • AI-assisted development tools: Claude, Manus AI, and ChatGPT.

We used simulated sensor data to represent astronaut physiological measurements and spacecraft environmental conditions during development and experimentation.

Creativity and Innovation:

The main innovative aspect of our project is connecting astronaut health monitoring with spacecraft environmental monitoring in one integrated platform. Instead of treating human health and spacecraft conditions as separate systems, our approach considers them as parts of one connected health ecosystem.

Another important feature is personalized health monitoring, combined with AI-based pattern analysis and an interactive astronaut visualization that uses color-coded indicators to make potential areas of concern easier to understand.

Factors Considered:

Our team considered the unique challenges of long-duration space missions, including space radiation, isolation, altered gravity, limited access to medical assistance, and environmental conditions inside the spacecraft.

We also considered individual health differences, the importance of monitoring changes over time, and the need to present complex AI analysis in a clear and understandable interface.

The platform is designed as a health monitoring and decision-support tool, not as a replacement for professional medical diagnosis or treatment.
